author: Quintus Ravel, Imperial Battlemage (retired)
pages:
#What Lies Behind the Gate

The first thing you notice is the heat. The second is the sky: red as a cut, and low, as if it were pressing down on the island you stand on.

The Deadlands are not one land but a scatter of black rock islands in a sea of fire. You cross from one to the next on bridges the Daedra built, and you do not look down.

#The Towers

On every island that matters there is a tower, taller than anything in the Imperial City. The Dremora call them sigil towers. At the top, past a hundred turns of a ramp, burns the stone that holds the gate open. A column of blood-red fire climbs the shaft at the tower's heart; brave fools ride it.

Take the stone, and the gate dies. The island throws you out like a bad tooth.

#Advice

The thorny vines they call harrada will open your legs to the bone. Walk around them.

Scamps are cowards; clannfear are not. A daedroth will breathe fire at you from further away than you think.

The red grass hides lava under its roots. Watch where the ground glows.
